title: Keep the analyzer working when source generation is suppressed

lines.text: > Note: When using Unity, dynamic code generation only works when targeting .NET Framework 4.x + mono runtime.
For all other Unity targets, AOT is required.
A `[MessagePackObject]` type can opt out of source generation with `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`.
No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which use reflection, so such a type is not AOT-safe.
The analyzer still validates these types, because they are serialized at run time and must still have a valid contract:
- Keys are unique and all of the same kind ([MsgPack005](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md)).
- Members have types that are themselves serializable ([MsgPack003](doc/analyzers/MsgPack003.md)).
- Types are accessible to the resolver ([MsgPack012](doc/analyzers/MsgPack012.md)).

The analyzer does not report the partial-class requirement ([MsgPack011](doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md)) or the AOT-only checks ([MsgPack016](doc/analyzers/MsgPack016.md) and [MsgPack017](doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md)) for these types, because they only apply when a formatter is generated.
You can customize the generated source through properties on the `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute`.
continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.
continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.
throw new InsufficientExecutionStackException($"This msgpack sequence has an object graph that exceeds the maximum depth allowed of {MaximumObjectGraphDepth}.");

/// Verifies that the analyzer keeps validating <c>[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]</c> types

// only matter when a formatter is generated, so they are not reported for a suppressed type.
public string Prop1 { get; init; } = ""some default"";

requirement.title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement.intent: The analyzer must report its diagnostics for types that set SuppressSourceGeneration = true, as it did in version 3.1.0.

functional.text: The analyzer reports diagnostics for a [MessagePackObject] type with SuppressSourceGeneration = true.
The analyzer behaves for such types as it did in version 3.1.0, before the regression in 3.1.1.

nonFunctional.text: The analyzer must not crash on invalid input in a suppressed type; it reports the problem instead. (inferred)
Types that do not suppress source generation keep their current diagnostics. (inferred)

expectedBehaviours: Compiling a project that has a [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] type with an analyzer-detectable problem, such as a public member missing a [Key] attribute, reports the matching MsgPack diagnostic.
The diagnostic points at the offending member or type in the suppressed type and has the same id and severity as it would for a type that does not suppress generation.
No formatter source is generated for the suppressed type, even though diagnostics are still reported for it.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a SuppressSourceGeneration = true type that has a member without a Key attribute expects the corresponding MsgPack diagnostic at that member.
A generator test confirms that no formatter is emitted for the suppressed type while the diagnostic is still reported.

expectedBehaviours: For suppressed types, the set of diagnostics (ids, locations, severities) matches what version 3.1.0 reported for the same input.
The 3.1.1 regression, where suppressed types got no diagnostics at all, no longer occurs.
Code that was valid under 3.1.0 gets no new diagnostics for suppressed types.
expectedTests: A regression test reproducing the MP-2234 scenario expects the same diagnostics that 3.1.0 produced.
A test with a valid suppressed type expects no diagnostics.

expectedBehaviours: A suppressed type with invalid input, such as duplicate keys, conflicting attributes or an unsupported member type, gets a diagnostic and does not throw an exception from the analyzer or generator.
The build output contains no AD0001 or CS8785 analyzer or generator failure warning for such input.
The rest of the compilation's diagnostics are still reported when one suppressed type is invalid.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a suppressed type that has duplicate key indexes expects the duplicate-key diagnostic and no analyzer exception diagnostic.
A test with a suppressed type whose member has an unresolvable or unsupported type expects a reported diagnostic and no crash.

expectedBehaviours: Types without SuppressSourceGeneration, or with it set to false, report exactly the same diagnostics as before the change.
Existing generator snapshot outputs under Resources stay unchanged for non-suppressed types.
Diagnostics are not reported twice for any type.
expectedTests: The existing analyzer and generator snapshot test suites pass unchanged.
A test with a mix of suppressed and non-suppressed types expects each diagnostic exactly once, at its expected location.

story.what: In both the property and field loops of TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo, the change stops adding a member to intMembers or stringMembers when that key is already there. It also skips a member with continue right after reporting the DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys diagnostic. Before, a duplicate key reached Dictionary.Add, which can throw. Now the KeysMustBeUnique or mixed-key diagnostic is reported and collection carries on. The change also loosens the depth check in MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep, documents SuppressSourceGeneration in the README, and adds analyzer and execution tests for suppressed types.
story.why: MP-2234 says the analyzer stopped reporting diagnostics for [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] types. The code shows invalid key input (duplicate or mixed keys) could throw while members were being collected. The diff does not show that this is the whole cause of the regression. The fix keeps reporting the problem and stops the crash. Generation is still skipped for suppressed types through the existing early return.

touches.note: Skips members whose key kind does not match the others, and guards dictionary adds against duplicate int or string keys in the property and field loops.
Depth check changed from >= to >, so a reader at exactly MaximumObjectGraphDepth no longer throws.
New execution tests: no generated formatter for a suppressed type, and a round trip through the dynamic resolver.
New analyzer tests for diagnostics on suppressed types, including duplicate and mixed keys.

findings.title: Unrelated change to the deserialization depth limit
findings.detail: MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep now throws only when reader.Depth is greater than MaximumObjectGraphDepth, not when it is equal. This allows one more level of nesting when reading untrusted payloads. MP-2234 is only about analyzer diagnostics for SuppressSourceGeneration types and does not cover this runtime limit. The doc comment just above still says the exception is thrown when the depth 'is already at or exceeds' the maximum, so it now disagrees with the code. No test in the change covers the new boundary.

findings.title: Field with Key(null) as first key still crashes analyzer
findings.detail: N1 says the analyzer must not crash on invalid input. Take a field whose [Key((string)null)] is the first keyed member, with no keyed property before it. BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull is reported and isIntKey becomes false. The mismatch check does not fire for the first member, so the code reaches the string branch and calls stringMembers.ContainsKey(stringKey!) with a null key. Dictionary throws ArgumentNullException, which shows up as AD0001 and hides the rest of the type's diagnostics. The property loop guards this with 'else if (stringKey is not null)', but the field loop does not. The new continue and ContainsKey guards leave this path open.

findings.title: Skipping mixed-key members also drops their member-type diagnostics
findings.detail: After DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys is reported, the new continue skips the rest of the loop body. That includes the recursive CollectCore(item.Type, item) call. Diagnostics about the member's own type, such as MsgPack003 when the type is not serializable, are therefore no longer reported for that member until the key kind is fixed. This affects suppressed and non-suppressed types alike, so the diagnostic set changes slightly for non-suppressed types (N2).

findings.title: No test for duplicate or mixed keys on fields
findings.detail: The change adds the same continue and ContainsKey guards to the field loop as to the property loop. All of the new MsgPack005 tests use properties only, so the field paths for duplicate int keys, duplicate string keys and mixed key kinds are not exercised. A regression there would bring back the analyzer crash.

findings.title: No test mixing suppressed and generated types in one compilation
findings.detail: N2 expects each diagnostic to be reported exactly once when suppressed and non-suppressed types appear together. Every new test has a single type, so there is no check against duplicated or missing diagnostics when both kinds of type are in the same compilation.

refusals.reason: The change loosens the MaximumObjectGraphDepth check used when reading untrusted payloads, which is a security design decision.
